article_title: Artificial intelligence in higher education: a systematic review of its impact on student engagement and the mediating role of teaching methods
citation: Long DY, Wang S, Md Rashid S and Lu XT. (2026). Artificial intelligence in higher education: a systematic review of its impact on student engagement and the mediating role of teaching methods. Front. Educ. 10:1648661. https://doi.org/10.3389/feduc.2025.1648661
title: PMAISE model: pedagogical mediation of AI for student engagement via structured feedback, interactive scaffolding, and personalization alignment
description: The PMAISE model (Pedagogical Mediation of AI for Student Engagement) is an inductively developed explanatory framework mapping the alignment between AI technologies, pedagogical strategies, and the affective, behavioral, and cognitive dimensions of engagement. Cross-case synthesis identified "three recurrent mechanisms: structured feedback, interactive scaffolding, and personalization alignment", which the authors say "constitute the core pathways through which pedagogical mediation operates in AI-supported higher education". The model frames AI tools as effective only when embedded in pedagogically sound designs.
requirements: AI functionalities must be aligned with instructional goals such as tailored feedback, structured interaction, and learner-centered adaptation
constraints: Inductively developed from the 73 included studies rather than tested as a hypothesis
target_learning_goals: cognitive, behavioral, and emotional engagement in AI-supported learning
examples: Figure 5 visualizes the model linking AIHE, pedagogical mediation strategies, learning tools, assessment approaches, and engagement dimensions
key_sources: Long DY, Wang S, Md Rashid S and Lu XT. (2026). Artificial intelligence in higher education: a systematic review of its impact on student engagement and the mediating role of teaching methods. Front. Educ. 10:1648661. https://doi.org/10.3389/feduc.2025.1648661

article_title: Using Bayesian networks to improve knowledge assessment
citation: Millán-Valldeperas, E.; Descalço, L.; Castillo, G.; Oliveira, P.; Diogo, S. (2013). Using Bayesian networks to improve knowledge assessment. Elsevier. http://hdl.handle.net/10630/7068
title: PMatE computerized testing system (Mathematics Education Project, University of Aveiro)
description: PMatE (Projecto Matemática Ensino) is an existing computerized testing system within the Mathematics Education Project of the University of Aveiro. In this study it served as the platform into which the generic Bayesian student model was integrated, delivering the computerized test that 152 students took alongside a written exam covering the same 12 concepts on first degree equations. Its test results fed a BSM whose diagnosis was compared with expert averages.
requirements: An existing testing platform delivering domain tests whose results can feed a Bayesian student model
constraints: Diagnosis from the computer-test BSM showed low agreement with the expert average in this evaluation
target_learners: students assessed in mathematics within the University of Aveiro's PMatE project
target_learning_goals: assessing student knowledge of first degree equations
examples: 152 students each took a computerized test within PMatE and a written exam designed to measure knowledge in 12 concepts related to first degree equations
key_sources: Millán-Valldeperas, E.; Descalço, L.; Castillo, G.; Oliveira, P.; Diogo, S. (2013). Using Bayesian networks to improve knowledge assessment. Elsevier. http://hdl.handle.net/10630/7068

article_title: Evaluation of "Back to Basics" Mathematics Workbooks: A Randomised Control Trial of the Primary Mathematics Research Project
citation: Brahm Fleisch, Nick Taylor, Roelien Herholdt and Ingrid Sapire. (2011). Evaluation of Back to Basics mathematics workbooks: a randomised control trial of the Primary Mathematics Research Project. South African Journal of Education, Vol 31:488-504. https://www.jet.org.za
title: Primary Mathematics Research Project (PMRP) Back to Basics workbook with diagnostic strand placement and daily mental maths
description: The PM material set is a learner workbook and teacher manual designed to move learners beyond unit counting and build automaticity in the four arithmetic operations. Teachers administer a diagnostic test and "place them into strands according to their achievement on the diagnostic test", with graded levels (Cow, Lion, Elephant, Goat) covering Grade 3 to Grade 6 level work on the same content. Each day starts with a 10 minute mental maths exercise; Day 5 lessons prescribe review, assessment, enrichment and remediation. The learner book is written in directly and is not amenable to self-study.
requirements: Requires teachers to test learners and place them in strands via the diagnostic test
Teacher guide and learner book must be used in tandem
constraints: Covers only LO1 (Number and operations), not the full curriculum
The graded-strand feature may make the book complex to use and makes it very bulky
target_learners: Grade 4-6 learners in South African primary schools serving low income communities
target_learning_goals: Proficiency in the four basic arithmetic operations
Place value and number concept understanding
examples: Used in the 2010 RCT across 22 Gauteng schools over a 14-week schedule
key_sources: Brahm Fleisch, Nick Taylor, Roelien Herholdt and Ingrid Sapire. (2011). Evaluation of Back to Basics mathematics workbooks: a randomised control trial of the Primary Mathematics Research Project. South African Journal of Education, Vol 31:488-504. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1136612

article_title: Effect of Conceptual Change Texts for Overcoming Misconceptions in "People and Management" Unit
citation: Orhan Dağdelen, İlker Kösterelioğlu. (2015). Effect of Conceptual Change Texts for Overcoming Misconceptions in “People and Management” Unit. International Electronic Journal of Elementary Education, 8(1), 99-112. https://www.iejee.com
title: People and Management Unit Achievement Test (PMAT)
description: The PMAT is the 18-item multiple-choice achievement test used to measure concept learning and misconceptions in the study. It was developed from a Concept Identification Form completed by 40 classroom teachers, reviewed by measurement experts, and piloted with 180 students. The article reports "Cronbach’s Alpha (a) reliability coefficient of the test was 0 .71 average discrimination of the test was 0.43 and average difficulty was 0.41".
requirements: Items were selected taking item difficulty and discrimination levels into account, with expert consultation for content and face validity.
target_learning_goals: Social studies concepts: constitution, independence, republic, democracy, government/state, public opinion, centralized administration, national sovereignty, local administration
examples: Administered as pre-test to eight 4th grade classrooms to select two classes with similar achievement levels.
key_sources: Orhan Dağdelen, İlker Kösterelioğlu. (2015). Effect of Conceptual Change Texts for Overcoming Misconceptions in “People and Management” Unit. International Electronic Journal of Elementary Education, 8(1), 99-112. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1078838

article_title: Improving the Reasoning Ability of Elementary School Student through the Indonesian Realistic Mathematics Education
citation: Saleh, M., Prahmana, R.C.I., Isa, M., & Murni. (2018). Improving the Reasoning Ability of Elementary School Student through the Indonesian Realistic Mathematics Education. Journal on Mathematics Education, 9(1), 41-54. https://jme.ejournal.unsri.ac.id
title: PMRI (Indonesian Realistic Mathematics Education) approach
description: PMRI is the Indonesian version of Realistic Mathematics Education, developed from the philosophy of RME, which "is viewed to be a potential approach to increase students' understanding of mathematics". In this paper its operational definition is "a learning which utilizes contextual problem and concrete object to understand concept and problem and to represent fraction based on the chosen context". Mathematics is thereby to be implemented in daily life activities, with students constructing knowledge actively through interaction with concrete objects and contextual problems.
requirements: Contextual problems chosen to stimulate learning activities toward the learning purposes
Concrete objects representing the mathematical content
Teacher acting as mentor and facilitator attending to students' concrete thinking stage
constraints: In this study applied to grade-4 fraction material, focusing on fraction as part of a whole
target_learners: Elementary school students in the concrete thinking stage
examples: The experiment used a chocolate-style fraction board and a local mortar (cobek) as the concrete objects within contextual fraction problems
key_sources: Saleh, M., Prahmana, R.C.I., Isa, M., & Murni. (2018). Improving the Reasoning Ability of Elementary School Student through the Indonesian Realistic Mathematics Education. Journal on Mathematics Education, 9(1), 41-54. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1173650

article_title: Reforming hospital management education with the P-MASE pedagogy: a randomized controlled trial.
citation: Zhang Yongshuo, Li Wenbo, Zhang Chuchen, Wang Yawei, Feng Shuo. (2026). Reforming hospital management education with the P-MASE pedagogy: a randomized controlled trial. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-08948-8
title: P-MASE: an integrated five-component pedagogy (Problem-based, Mobile, Authentic, Social, Experiential) for hospital management education
description: P-MASE is a descriptive acronym for a bundled pedagogy combining problem-based learning, mobile learning, authentic learning, social learning, and experiential learning. It "organizes job-relevant management competencies into authentic, cross-department task chains, supports learning through mobile/digital tools and collaboration, and aligns assessment with management performance evidence collected across tasks." Its novelty lies in integrating what to learn, how to learn, and how to judge performance into one coherent design logic, targeting systems thinking and trade-off reasoning.
requirements: Interdisciplinary teaching teams spanning management, clinical, and informatics expertise
Digital infrastructure: SuperStar platform, virtual simulation platform, Power BI, AnyLogic modeling, and NLP tools
constraints: The study evaluated P-MASE as an integrated package and was not designed to estimate component-specific effects or isolate individual components
target_learners: undergraduate Health Administration and Information Resource Management students
target_learning_goals: hospital management competencies including policy interpretation, data-driven decision making, crisis communication, and systems thinking
examples: Semi-structured interviews at eight tertiary hospitals identified six categories of authentic management problems (e.g., DRG cost overruns, ICU infection rates) feeding a four-stage problem-solving workflow
Students completed departmental rotations in Operations, Quality Control, and Outpatient Services using Power BI to analyze surgical efficiency
key_sources: Zhang Yongshuo, Li Wenbo, Zhang Chuchen, Wang Yawei, Feng Shuo. (2026). Reforming hospital management education with the P-MASE pedagogy: a randomized controlled trial. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-08948-8

article_title: Reforming hospital management education with the P-MASE pedagogy: a randomized controlled trial.
citation: Zhang Yongshuo, Li Wenbo, Zhang Chuchen, Wang Yawei, Feng Shuo. (2026). Reforming hospital management education with the P-MASE pedagogy: a randomized controlled trial. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-08948-8
title: Combined evaluation framework integrating data-driven metrics, simulation modeling, and NLP for performance-based assessment
description: The study used a four-dimensional evaluation indicator system (Theoretical Knowledge, Skills Ability, Learning Process, Teaching Satisfaction) with ten indicators, mapping course objectives to assessment methods. Tools included a closed-book exam, simulation sandbox scoring, RoBERTa-based NLP analysis of empathy expressions and discussion sentiment, DRG clustering accuracy against a reference standard, Simio simulation of emergency resource allocation, and LMS log indicators. The framework yields "measurable and reusable competency assessments" of learners' reasoning within standardized tasks.
requirements: Locally developed NLP (RoBERTa) model and simulation platforms
An objective-to-assessment mapping aligning each course objective with specific assessment methods
constraints: The NLP model and simulation platforms were locally developed and have not undergone extensive external validation across diverse datasets or institutions
Indicators represent educational performance measures, not real-world hospital operational outcomes
target_learning_goals: applied reasoning and decision-making competencies in hospital management
examples: DRG grouping accuracy assessed against a reference standard as an indicator of rule application and data interpretation
AHP-enabled multi-criteria structuring of trade-offs in budgeting/resource-allocation simulations
key_sources: Zhang Yongshuo, Li Wenbo, Zhang Chuchen, Wang Yawei, Feng Shuo. (2026). Reforming hospital management education with the P-MASE pedagogy: a randomized controlled trial. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-026-08948-8

article_title: Perceived Medical School stress of undergraduate medical students predicts academic performance: an observational study.
citation: Kötter T, Wagner J, Brüheim L, Voltmer E. (2017). Perceived Medical School stress of undergraduate medical students predicts academic performance: an observational study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-017-1091-0
title: Perceived Medical School Stress Instrument (PMSS / PMSS-D), a 13-item questionnaire covering workload, competition, social isolation and financial worries
description: The PMSS is the most widespread validated stress questionnaire designed for use in Medical School, introduced by Vitaliano et al. and adapted into German (PMSS-D) and other languages. It "addresses a wide range of possible stressors, including workload, competition, social isolation and financial worries"; each of the 13 items is answered on a five-point Likert scale and summed (range 13–65). The study used the German 13-item version at two time points.
requirements: Completion via survey (here web-based SurveyMonkey); scoring allows substitution of up to one missing item by the mean of the other 12 before computing the sum score
constraints: A systematic review of stress-management programs recommends the PMSS among the standard outcome measures for that research area; the article notes other stress instruments' heterogeneity prohibits direct comparison of results
target_learning_goals: identifying students at risk of poor academic performance
examples: In this study the PMSS-D was administered at the end of freshman year (T1) and end of sophomore year (T2) via web-based SurveyMonkey and matched to M1 grades
key_sources: Kötter T, Wagner J, Brüheim L, Voltmer E. (2017). Perceived Medical School stress of undergraduate medical students predicts academic performance: an observational study. BMC Medical Education. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12909-017-1091-0
